description: Returns the reading records the HTMLRadar website exports as a spreadsheet, as CSV text: for readers shown in full, one row per section per read (a read with no section recorded has one row with the section columns blank; section_status says "not measured" when the page changed while it was being read, so no section time was taken), with the link's label and slug, the reader, whether their address was verified, when they opened it, how long they read, how far they scrolled, and their country and device where recorded; proved_by says how each read got in (code, microsoft, google, password, address, personal, open or "not recorded") and signed_in_at when that sign-in happened (blank where there was none or it was not recorded); read_version, the last column, is the version of the page the read began on (a number, "live page" for a hosted page, blank where it was not recorded). On Free, the first five readers of a link are shown in full; later readers appear in a "more read it" count row without their individual details. The sender's own previews and internal viewers are left out, as on the website. With `share_id`, the records cover one link; without it every link of the document is included. A very long answer is cut at a whole record and gives a `continue_from` value for the remaining rows. The website file itself holds only the oldest 5,000 reads of a document or link, and the result says when it is every row of that file and when the file is capped. It changes nothing. It is the full export; get_share_activity summarises one link.

continue_from.description: The `continue_from` value a previous answer gave selects the rows after it. Omission starts from the first row.

document_id.description: The document: the document id from list_documents or list_shares.

share_id.description: Limit the records to one link: the share id, the share's slug, or the link itself.

name: get_reading_records
title: Get a document's reading records
